heading: Xiao Jing 孝經 · The Hsiao King, or Classic of Filial Piety · Xiao Jing 1 · The Scope and Meaning of the Treatise … Filial Piety in Relation to the Three Powers

items.text: Do not injure or wound your body, for it is received from your parents.
items.quote: Our bodies--to every hair and bit of skin--are received by us from our parents, and we must not presume to injure or wound them.

items.text: Establish your character and make your name famous to glorify your parents.
items.quote: make our name famous in future ages, and thereby glorify our parents.

items.text: Ever think of your ancestor and cultivate your virtue.
items.quote: Ever think of your ancestor, Cultivating your virtue.

items.text: Serve your parents with utmost love and reverence.
items.quote: the love and reverence (of the Son of Heaven) are thus carried to the utmost in the service of his parents.

items.text: Preserve your ancestral temples.
items.quote: they can then preserve their ancestral temples.
items.conflict: Worship of ancestors is forbidden; honor memory without offerings (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Serve your father with love and reverence.
items.quote: both of these things are given to the father.

items.text: Serve your mother with love.
items.quote: love is what is chiefly rendered to the mother.

items.text: Maintain the ancestral sacrifices.
items.quote: maintain their sacrifices.
items.conflict: Sacrifices to the dead are idolatrous; Christ is the only mediator (1 Tim 2:5).

items.text: Nourish your parents.
items.quote: in order to nourish their parents.

items.text: Avoid being hated or contemned by others, for your conduct reflects on your parents.
items.quote: He who loves his parents will not dare (to incur the risk of) being hated by any man... contemned by any man.

heading: Xiao Jing 孝經 · The Hsiao King, or Classic of Filial Piety · Xiao Jing 8 · Filial Piety in Government … Amplification of 'The All-Embracing Rule of Conduct'

items.text: Do not slight her; give her honor above servants and concubines.
items.quote: The heads of clans did not dare to slight their servants and concubines;--how much less would they slight their wives and sons!

items.text: Do not slight him; give him honor above servants and concubines.
items.quote: The heads of clans did not dare to slight their servants and concubines;--how much less would they slight their wives and sons!

items.text: Revere your father with awe; in filial piety nothing is greater.
items.quote: In filial piety there is nothing greater than the reverential awe of one's father.

items.text: Offer the border-altar sacrifice to the founding ancestor, and in the Brilliant Hall sacrifice to your father as the correlate of God.
items.quote: at the border altar sacrificed to Hâu-kî as the correlate of Heaven, and in the Brilliant Hall he honoured king Wăn, and sacrificed to him as the correlate of God.
items.conflict: Ancestral sacrifice and making a father 'correlate of God' exalts a creature; Scripture forbids worshiping anyone but God (Exod 20:3-5; Deut 4:15-19).

items.text: Love and revere your parents above all other people; do not love or revere others more than them.
items.quote: he who does not love his parents, but loves other men, is called a rebel against virtue

items.text: In your general conduct to them, manifest the utmost reverence.
items.quote: In his general conduct to them, he manifests the utmost reverence.

items.text: In nourishing them, give them the utmost pleasure.
items.quote: in his nourishing of them, his endeavour is to give them the utmost pleasure.

items.text: When they are ill, feel the greatest anxiety and care for them.
items.quote: when they are ill, he feels the greatest anxiety.

items.text: In mourning for them dead, exhibit every demonstration of grief.
items.quote: in mourning for them (dead), he exhibits every demonstration of grief.

items.text: When sacrificing to them, display the utmost solemnity.
items.quote: in sacrificing to them, he displays the utmost solemnity.
items.conflict: Ancestral sacrifice is idolatry; the dead cannot receive offerings and God forbids necromancy (Deut 18:10-12; Isa 8:19).

items.text: Be submissive and observe propriety toward your elder sibling; this is fraternal duty.
items.quote: for teaching them (the observance of) propriety and submissiveness there is nothing better than Fraternal Duty.

heading: Xiao Jing 孝經 · The Hsiao King, or Classic of Filial Piety · Xiao Jing 13 · Amplification of 'The Perfect Virtue' … Filial Piety in Mourning for Parents

items.text: Remonstrate with your father when he is doing unrighteousness; do not blindly obey his orders.
items.quote: when a case of unrighteous conduct is concerned, a son must by no means keep from remonstrating with his father

items.text: Serve your parents with love and reverence.
items.quote: I have heard your instructions on the affection of love, on respect and reverence

items.text: Give repose to the minds of your parents; do not cause them anxiety.
items.quote: giving repose to (the minds of) our parents

items.text: Make your name famous so as to bring honor to your parents.
items.quote: on making our name famous

items.text: Serve your elder brother with fraternal duty, showing submission and deference.
items.quote: the fraternal duty with which he serves his elder brother

items.text: Mourn for your parent with grief and sorrow, but do not let it harm your life; let the mourning period not exceed three years.
items.quote: The period of mourning does not go beyond three years, to show the people that it must have an end.

items.text: Bury your parent properly with inner and outer coffins and grave clothes, and escort the body sorrowfully to the grave.
items.quote: An inner and outer coffin are made; the grave-clothes also are put on, and the shroud; and (the body) is lifted (into the coffin). ... they sorrowfully escort the coffin to the grave.

items.text: Consult the tortoise-shell to determine the grave site for your parent.
items.quote: They consult the tortoise-shell to determine the grave and the ground about it
items.conflict: Trusting in divination conflicts with the biblical prohibition on divination (Deuteronomy 18:10).

items.text: Offer sacrifices in the ancestral temple in spring and autumn, presenting offerings to the spirit of your parent.
items.quote: In spring and autumn they offer sacrifices, thinking of the deceased as the seasons come round.
items.conflict: Offering sacrifices to the dead conflicts with the biblical prohibition on venerating the dead and with the finality of Christ's sacrifice.

items.text: Cultivate your person and be careful of your conduct, fearing lest you disgrace your ancestors.
items.quote: he cultivates his person and is careful of his conduct, fearing lest he should disgrace his predecessors.

items.text: Honor your uncles.
items.quote: he must have some whom he honours; that is, he has his uncles of his surname

items.text: Yield precedence to your elder cousins.
items.quote: He must have some to whom he concedes the precedence; that is, he has his cousins, who bear the same surname, and are older than himself.
